title: Find the invoices a bank payment file did not settle
examObjective: Defining, using, and reusing DataWeave modules, functions, and variables
basics: `leftJoin(left, right, leftKey, rightKey)` from `dw::core::Arrays` pairs every element of `left` with the matching elements of `right`. Each result is `{ l, r }`, and a left element with no match comes back with no `r` at all, which is how you find the unmatched ones.
prompt:
Accounts receives `{ invoices, payments }`: open invoices `{ id, amount }` and the day's bank payments `{ invoiceId, paid }`. Return the ids of the invoices that no payment refers to, in invoice order.

The bank file is generated from a text export, so `invoiceId` sometimes arrives as a String (`"101"`) even though invoice ids are Numbers.
hints: You are looking for left rows with no match on the right: a left join, then keep the pairs with no `r`.
A lookup with `contains` compares type as well as value. What happens when the payment says `"102"`?
`leftJoin(payload.invoices, payload.payments, (i) -> i.id, (p) -> p.invoiceId) filter ($.r == null) map $.l.id`, with `default []` for the case where everything is paid.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
import * from dw::core::Arrays
---
(leftJoin(payload.invoices, payload.payments, (i) -> i.id, (p) -> p.invoiceId) filter ($.r == null)).l.id default []

mustFail.why: checks the payment ids with contains, which compares types, so a payment that quotes the id as text settles nothing
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
(payload.invoices filter not (payload.payments.invoiceId contains $.id)).id default []

mustFail.why: uses an inner join, which returns the paid invoices instead of the unpaid ones
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
import * from dw::core::Arrays
---
join(payload.invoices, payload.payments, (i) -> i.id, (p) -> p.invoiceId).l.id default []

explanation.approach: The unmatched rows are exactly what a left join exposes, as pairs without an `r`. The join also compares its keys as text, so the Number 101 and the String "101" match, which a `contains` check does not do. An invoice paid in two parts produces two pairs, but both have an `r`, so it is still correctly left out.

snippets.label: contains compares types
snippets.note: The String does not equal the Number.

snippets.label: A join does not
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
import * from dw::core::Arrays
---
sizeOf(join([{ id: 102 }], [{ invoiceId: "102" }], (i) -> i.id, (p) -> p.invoiceId))

snippets.label: An unmatched pair
snippets.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
import * from dw::core::Arrays
---
leftJoin([{ id: 104 }], [], (i) -> i.id, (p) -> p.invoiceId)
